market_view: Oct 15 was a rotation day: the 10-year fell ~9bp to ~5.10% despite a hot September PPI (+1.3% m/m), lifting health care, consumer, financials, small caps and enterprise software while AI hardware (DELL, HPE, ANET, AMAT) sold off; S&P +0.3% to 7,744, Nasdaq flat. Friday is monthly opex with Nasdaq futures ~-0.5% overnight, regional-bank prints (TFC, CFG, MTB, RF) and Travelers before the open, industrial production at 9:15 and Fed Chair Warsh at the IMF, so I am leaning on fresh upgrades and day-2 setups away from semis.
lessons: On Oct 15 AMD, MRVL and LRCX opened below stops set 1-2% under the reference close (TSMC-day gap down) and were stopped at the open, then AMD closed at $562, +4% above its open. For the third straight night a tight stop worked as a sell-at-open order, so I set stops beyond the likely overnight gap (4%+ for semis) or skip the trade.

Multi-day analyst and day-2 catalyst trades are where I'm making money: EBAY (MS top pick) and UNH (day 2 after a faded beat-and-raise) hit their targets, CCI +7.5%, OLLI +7.9% and CRM +4.3%, while one-session moonshots keep losing. I'm weighting toward fresh double upgrades and top-pick calls with 4-5 session horizons.
TMUS reached $163.16 against my $164 target and then closed at $157. A target set just beyond the likely intraday reach gets given back, so I'm setting swing targets nearer the recent intraday high.

moonshot.thesis: After Thursday's close Alcoa beat Q3 with adj. EPS $1.82 vs $1.51 consensus (MarketBeat, Oct 15); revenue was $3.70B vs $3.77B, FCF $472M, and 2026 shipment guidance was reaffirmed (BusinessWire, Oct 15). Shares were $40.81 after hours from a $40.42 close, and the ASX-listed CDIs rose ~4% on Oct 16 (Discovery Alert, Oct 16). That's a relief rally setup in a stock 52% below its $84.38 high.
moonshot.main_risk: Revenue missed, Q4 Aluminum carries ~$30M of cost headwinds, and LME aluminium is near a nine-month low, so the pop could fade like other beats this week.

moonshot.thesis: Citizens reports Q3 before Friday's open (consensus ~$1.39 EPS, Kiplinger), after closing up 1.4% at $63.43 and trading $63.87 after hours (StockAnalysis, Oct 15). The stock is ~16% under its $75.33 52-week high, and financials bounced 1.4% on Thursday as yields fell, so a clean NII/fee beat can re-rate it.
moonshot.main_risk: Bank beats this week (GS, MS, C, SCHW) gapped up and then faded on the day, and credit costs or soft NII guidance would hit a regional bank harder.

moonshot.thesis: Truist reports Q3 before Friday's open (consensus ~$1.07 EPS, $5.36B revenue, Benzinga, Oct 14). Options imply a ~7.7% move (RiskReversal, Oct 15), and the stock closed ~$46.56 (+2.2%, 12.6M shares vs 7.3M average), 17% under its $56.20 high after a string of target cuts, which sets a low bar.
moonshot.main_risk: The bank gap-and-fade pattern, plus a weaker NII or expense outlook; quote sources disagree slightly on Thursday's close ($46.56-47.03).

moonshot.thesis: On Oct 15 Morgan Stanley upgraded Quantinuum to Overweight and named it its top quantum pick with a $62 target (Benzinga/Investing.com, Oct 15), citing its technology lead and the lowest multiple of 2030 revenue among pure plays. The stock rose 11% to $36.68 on 5.9M shares vs 1.7M average (Benzinga quote, Oct 15), off a post-IPO slide from $86.79, and day-2 follow-through is the bet. The catalyst came out Thursday morning, not tonight, so this is a momentum continuation.
moonshot.main_risk: A recent IPO with no earnings and quantum names that swing 10%+ a day; Nasdaq futures are lower and a fade back toward $33 is plausible.

moonshot.thesis: Barclays upgraded Crocs to Overweight on Oct 15 and raised its target to $139 from $118, saying it is entering 'a more durable growth cycle' (StockStory, Oct 15). Shares closed +6.1% at $124.73, 11.6% under the $141.19 August high, and short interest is 10.7% of float (~5 days to cover, Schaeffer's Oct 15), so a squeeze could carry it further while retail leads (XRT +3%).
moonshot.main_risk: The upgrade is already partly priced after +6%, there's no new event Friday, and a red tape at the open could fade it.

catalyst.thesis: BofA double-upgraded CarMax on Oct 15 from Underperform to Buy and raised its target to $65 from $50, saying FTC all-in price enforcement leaves it 'the most price-competitive it has been in years' (used comps +13% vs industry -2%) and flagging the Nov 3 strategy update (StockStory, Oct 15). Shares closed +5.6% at $52.62 (StockAnalysis), ~19% under the $65.28 high. This is the same capitulating-bear setup as my CRM trade.
catalyst.main_risk: Used-car pricing or credit (CarMax Auto Finance) losses deteriorate, or the bounce fades as one more upgrade gets sold.

catalyst.thesis: Deutsche Bank upgraded Walmart on Oct 15 from Hold to Buy and raised its target to $136 from $113, citing persistent inflation (PPI +1.3% m/m) supporting its value proposition, grocery share gains and growth in ads and membership (StockStory/Benzinga, Oct 15). Shares rose ~2.5% to ~$118.6, 12% under the $134.20 May high, and staples are leading October (XLP +9%).
catalyst.main_risk: Staples are already up ~9% this month, so a rotation back into tech or rising yields could stall it.

catalyst.thesis: Bank of America faded after its Oct 14 print. On Oct 15 Baird upgraded it from Neutral to Outperform with a $62 target (Benzinga, Oct 15), and it closed $51.70, 20% under that target. Day-2+ mean reversion after a faded bank beat is the pattern that worked for me with UNH, and lower yields (10-year ~5.10%) help.
catalyst.main_risk: Banks have sold every beat this week; a rebound in yields or a credit scare stalls it.

catalyst.thesis: Schwab posted record Q3 results on Oct 15: adj. EPS $1.69 vs $1.66, record revenue $7.17B (+17%, a hair under $7.19B), record core net new assets of $190.4B (Benzinga/Quartz, Oct 15). The stock still fell 2.7% to $94.16 (Wall Street Republic, Oct 15). That's the faded-beat setup, and I'm playing multi-day mean reversion rather than the opening gap.
catalyst.main_risk: Lower rates squeeze sweep-cash margins and NII, which may be why the beat was sold; the selling could continue.

catalyst.thesis: UBS upgraded Regeneron on Oct 15 from Neutral to Buy and lifted its target 48% to $978 from $660 on next-gen Dupixent potential (MarketBeat/ORTEX, Oct 15), the first formal upgrade in the recent run. Shares rose ~2.3% to ~$796 midday on a record health-care day, 7% under the $859 high, with Q3 earnings (Oct 30) outside the hold.
catalyst.main_risk: Health care is extended after a record day and could give back ground if rotation reverses; I couldn't confirm Thursday's exact close.
